CHIEF COMPLAINT
Evaluation of kidney stones and follow-up of hypertension and diabetes.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Angela presents for evaluation of recurrent kidney stones. She reports this is approximately her 7th or 8th episode of kidney stones. She presented to the emergency room last week with pain that has since improved. She believes the stone passed approximately 3 days ago. She denies current hematuria and denies current pain. She received Percocet at the emergency room for pain management. She was previously evaluated by a urologist approximately one year ago.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies chest pain or abdominal pain. She reports history of insomnia with occasional nighttime worry; she has tried meditation apps with some benefit. She denies current hematuria and pain related to kidney stones.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
- Hypertension
- Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (diagnosed approximately one year ago)
- Recurrent kidney stones (7-8 episodes)
- Grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur (previously known, unchanged)
- Insomnia

MEDICATIONS
- Norvasc 2.5 mg daily
- Metformin 500 mg daily
- Melatonin (used occasionally with minimal benefit)

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient reports difficulty with dietary management, particularly consuming fast food, cakes, and cookies due to time constraints with work and meal preparation. For sleep, patient sleeps with television on and keeps phone by bedside in case of calls. Does not currently use sleep mode feature on phone.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: Blood pressure 150/90 at visit. Home blood pressure readings 130-140/60-70 taken 2-3 times per week.
Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally, no crackles
Heart: Grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur, unchanged from prior
Abdomen: Soft, no tenderness to palpation
Costovertebral angles: No tenderness bilaterally

RESULTS
A1C: 6.7 (improved from baseline at diagnosis one year ago)

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Recurrent kidney stones: Patient appears to have passed current stone. Will obtain urinalysis and urine culture. Referral to urology (Dr. Harris) for evaluation of recurrent stone formation and preventive measures.

2. Hypertension: Well-controlled on Norvasc 2.5 mg daily. Home readings reassuring for adequate control; white coat syndrome likely contributing to elevated office reading. No medication changes. Refills provided.

3. Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: Continue Metformin 500 mg daily. Patient counseled to check blood glucose before each meal to gauge appropriate food intake. A1C of 6.7 shows improvement from diagnosis but remains slightly elevated.

4. Nutrition: Referral to dietitian for dietary counseling. Goal to reduce sodium intake to less than 2300 mg per day and optimize diet to potentially reduce medication requirements.

5. Insomnia: Start melatonin 10 mg as needed. Counsel on sleep hygiene including avoiding electronics before bed, keeping room dark and cool, and utilizing sleep mode on phone to minimize notifications.

6. Follow-up: Return in 3 months for reassessment.
